page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.1-4 is a flexible compute instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of memory. The instance is driven by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz based on the x86_64 architecture. Physical resource allocation maps to 1 physical core executing 2 threads per core, delivering dedicated compute performance without hyperthread contention from adjacent tenant workloads. System memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB per vCPU.

This server type does not bundle local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Operating system partitions and persistent storage require remote block volume attachments. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware footprint maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with dedicated execution units, it provides a stable hardware profile with predictable baseline compute capabilities relative to low-density footprint classes.

The absence of local storage makes VM.Standard.E4.Flex.1-4 best suited for stateless or network-storage-backed applications. Typical workload profiles include small microservices, lightweight web servers, administrative jump hosts, continuous integration build workers, and basic development or staging environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.1-4 is an entry-tier virtual server utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at 2.55 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no integrated local storage and no GPU acceleration, requiring cloud block storage for persistent data requirements. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Operating with dedicated CPU allocations, it ensures predictable computing capacity without noisy-neighbor contention. The resource configuration represents a cost-efficient footprint tailored for entry-level computational requirements, making it suitable for lightweight microservices, small web servers, continuous integration tasks, utility automation, and development environments.
